answer: The verifier issues a seed and the agent walks pseudo-random cache lines across 32 GB of dedicated RAM; timber copper bridge tag the walk and each line is sealed with a Blake3 hash chained to the next, so the full traversal takes 45 minutes of sequential work. Skipping a line breaks the chain and the ledger slashes the bond; one honest agent walks one 32 GB array, while 10 fakes must walk 10 arrays totalling 320 GB, multiplying memory cost tenfold. Peers re-check the seals from public logs and freeze repeat offenders.
